prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 个人所得税专项附加扣除标准简表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "扣除项目" spans 1 col × 2 row; "每月标准（元）" spans 2 col × 1 row; "适用条件" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "扣除项目" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 133px
  col 2: header "每月标准（元） › 一般地区" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 203px
  col 3: header "每月标准（元） › 特殊情形" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 435px
  col 4: header "适用条件" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 1038px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 440px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 439px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [85, 85, 78, 191] · table 440×1151px · row heights [36, 60, 246, 153, 176, 153, 153, 176] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 10 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [85, 85, 100, 169] · table 440×1198px · row heights [36, 36, 176, 153, 199, 199, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [94, 85, 91, 169] · table 440×1198px · row heights [36, 36, 176, 153, 199, 199, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [88, 82, 89, 180] · table 440×1128px · row heights [36, 60, 176, 153, 176, 176, 176, 176] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [92, 80, 96, 171] · table 440×1221px · row heights [36, 60, 176, 153, 199, 199, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [94, 85, 89, 171] · table 440×1198px · row heights [36, 36, 176, 153, 199, 199, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [92, 85, 85, 177] · table 440×1151px · row heights [36, 36, 199, 153, 176, 176, 176, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [90, 85, 94, 170] · table 440×1198px · row heights [36, 36, 176, 153, 199, 199, 199, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3B"],"acceptable":["r1C","r2A","r2B","r2C","r3A","r3C"],"bad":[{"design":"r1B","why":"特殊情形列过窄，表头换行，首条内容被挤成十行，拉高首个数据行并削弱两列标准的并排比较。"}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[91,93],[85,85],[84,86],[176,178]],"rationale":"r3B 的两级表头均保持单行，读者可以先辨认扣除项目，再横向比较一般地区和特殊情形。适用条件获得较宽的空间，长说明的行长和各数据行的高度较为均衡；特殊情形列虽有较多换行，仍能与对应条件保持清晰的行关联。","principles":{"general":["根据内容的作用和长度分配宽度，同时保留相关列之间的比较关系。","评估换行时应看整行的阅读节奏和表头层级，而非只看表格总高度。"],"specific":["本表的适用条件是最长的连续说明，需要占据最大宽度。","两列每月标准需要足够宽以保持子表头完整，同时为条件说明留出空间。"]},"tradeoffs":"r2B 的条件列更宽，数据行更紧凑，但一般地区表头换成两行；偏重说明阅读的设计师可能更喜欢它。r1C 则给特殊情形更多空间，代价是条件说明更窄、部分行更高。","uncertain":"范围是依据所给渲染结果作出的保守估计，不是对每个像素宽度的浏览器实测；调整某一列时需按其他列比例重新分配宽度，并保持总宽不超过439px。"}
